items.prose: Horizontal slip along the regional strike-slip fault registered magnitude 4.2 at 14.5 kilometers depth. The shear wave triggered the automated hydraulic interlocks on Blast Door 2, slamming eighteen tons of steel shut in two-point-four seconds.

A continuous monochromatic 1.8 Hz harmonic tremor recorded for seventy-two hours. Telemetry indicates a shallow magma body inflating three kilometers below the caldera. Groundwater temperature in the sump well rose fourteen degrees in twenty-four hours.

A sharp, high-frequency compressional P-wave arrival with virtually zero shear wave tail—the unmistakable seismic signature of a 150-kiloton deep underground nuclear detonation. Epicenter triangulated to the abandoned missile proving grounds three hundred kilometers north.

Catastrophic roof fall in the flooded anthracite coal workings of Sector 6. The sudden collapse of four square kilometers of unsupported galleries produced a sharp atmospheric pressure pulse that blew out ventilation duct inspection covers across three shelter levels.

A swarm of eighty micro-earthquakes within two hours following high-pressure brine injection into the deep heat-exchange borehole. Induced fracturing cracked the impermeable cap rock, allowing scalding mineral water to flood into the Level 5 drainage adit.

Piezoresistive quartz strain gauges embedded in the main bunker support pillars saturated at 4,000 micro-strain. Concrete core samples show microscopic diagonal shear cracks forming along the structural load-bearing archways of Sector 1.

The continental plate, rebounding rapidly as miles of surface ice sublimated into volcanic winter clouds, sheared along an ancient Precambrian fault. The bunker shifted eight millimeters vertically, snapping cast-iron sewage drainage pipes across three sectors.

High-amplitude ground shock confirming the successful subterranean launch of an automated nuclear-tipped communication rocket from Silo 04. The seismic pulse was registered by surviving monitoring arrays across forty thousand square kilometers of empty continent.
